headline: Google DeepMind has developed a way to hide a watermark in AI-designed proteins without stopping them working, but the mark can be scrubbed.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: DeepMind announced SynthID Bio on 30 Sep 2026, before the window, and this explainer adds no new facts about the work.
importance_line: Biosecurity screeners and protein designers could get a way to tell AI-designed proteins from natural ones, but the mark can be removed, cannot name who made a protein, and there is no agreement on who should hold the key that reads it.
summary: Singularity Hub reports that Google DeepMind has developed SynthID Bio, announced on 30 Sep 2026, a method that hides a subtle watermark in AI-designed proteins so they can later be recognised and that, in lab tests, watermarked protein binders (molecules built to latch onto a target protein) worked as well as unmarked ones. The article adds that the mark can be removed by running a protein through another design tool and cannot yet identify who made a protein, and that Oliver Crook of the University of Oxford told Science it could add complexity for researchers whose work raises no safety concern.
